findings.claim: Across the full observed window (score times 0.0-0.49, 14 independent batches), the strongest whole-window coordinate contrasts are negative in the local_cyy (y-y covariance) components of several landmarks, led by landmark_16_local_cyy (whole_window_z=-0.672) and landmark_07_local_cyy (whole_window_z=-0.646), with landmark_19_local_cyy and landmark_08_local_cyy also negative. These are endpoint-world coordinate features, not affinity labels.

The same negative whole-window cyy contrasts show a sign-changing rate structure: first_rate_z is strongly negative and last_rate_z is positive (e.g. landmark_16_local_cyy first_rate_z=-42.6, last_rate_z=+25.0; landmark_07_local_cyy first_rate_z=-24.3, last_rate_z=+14.4), with 3 sign changes and no accepted polynomial. This indicates a changing regional direction rather than a stationary target, and the derivative does not by itself specify an absolute coordinate target.

A positive whole-window contrast appears in landmark_00_soft_mass (whole_window_z=+0.639), also with sign-changing rates (first_rate_z=+9.3, last_rate_z=-10.0, 4 sign changes, one strong sign conflict). This is a soft-mass occupancy proxy, not a typed chemical or energy quantity.

The learning window and score clocks are fixed at [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing, and the objective is final predicted target affinity primary with coordinate control only; recorded affinities were removed and the score prior is equal, so selection/survival evidence is not decoded final affinity.

hypotheses.direction: Test S1 (observed-to-static) versus S2 (constant blend) and S3 (static-to-observed) at fixed dose; do not reverse the affinity objective
hypotheses.falsifier: If S1, S2 and S3 produce indistinguishable endpoint-affinity and coordinate-contrast traces at matched score nodes, the staged-relevance hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: Per-score-node teacher_blend applied to the endpoint reward scalar, with delta_A and dose_factors held at 1.0
hypotheses.scope: All seeds over the full learning window [0.0,0.5]; reward lane only
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent teacher-relevance reward (early same-clock historical forecast teachers smoothly approaching frozen static teachers, as in the offered S1 recipe) merits testing at fixed dose against the constant-blend control S2 and the reversed control S3, because the observed cyy contrasts change sign across the window rather than holding a stationary direction.

hypotheses.direction: Test a smooth delta_A(t) only under a registered curvature condition; retain gradual change absent a reproducible knot
hypotheses.falsifier: If a constant delta_A matches the staged delta_A on endpoint affinity and coordinate contrasts, the time-varying curvature is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: delta_A(t) applied to the Hungarian-matched endpoint MSD kernel
hypotheses.scope: Seeds showing the strongest cyy sign change; curvature conditions only
hypotheses.statement: The negative whole-window cyy contrasts with sign-changing rates suggest the geometric response scale (delta_A) may need to differ between early and late phases, but this is a diagnostic of changing contrast, not evidence for an absolute coordinate target or a discovered stage boundary.

limitations: No temporal profiles are available (temporal_profiles_available=false); unqueried is not unavailable, and no stage boundary can be inferred from missing profiles.
All continuous_trends rows report polynomial_accepted=false and extrapolation_allowed=false, so no extrapolation beyond the observed window is supported.
The coordinate features are untyped endpoint-world proxies; no energy, chemical-interaction or neural-module interpretation is warranted.
Selection preference and survival are not decoded final affinity; recorded affinities were removed, so no descendant-benefit claim is made.
The offered S1/S2/S3 recipes are predeclared interventions, not discovered biological stages.
